decision.rule: pre-registered (cycle 24 N3) and NOT a new rule — it is D6's rule verbatim, applied to the dossier's unmet conditions E/F/G. The dossier: 'Keep a learner only if its removal causes at least a 5% decline in one target metric without improving another more important metric.' Operationally as D6 applied it: a learner keeps its place on EITHER its welfare removal cost OR its own documented skill metric, at the same 5% bar. Skill baselines follow existing D6 precedents rather than new statistics: regret reduction vs a uniform random policy (the animation_bandit precedent), return improvement vs a DEPTH-1 STUMP (the tree's own simpler self — if depth 2 cannot beat depth 1 the second split is decoration), and next-interaction Brier reduction vs the running interaction rate (the attention_forecast precedent, the harsher baseline). DROPPING ALL THREE IS FIRST-CLASS. The incumbent eleven are RE-JUDGED on the new full_fleet baseline, because adding threads moves the baseline every removal cost is measured against and a changed kept-five roster would be a real result about the fleet.
